equity_bridge.item: Tariff refund cash on the balance sheet not retained by owners (reinvestment commitment + tax)
equity_bridge.note: 383 of refund cash incl. interest received by 2026-08-01 is inside cash; management guides a net benefit of ~$0.60/share (~115 after tax on ~191M average shares). The 268 difference is tax on the refund and the reinvestment being spent in H2, neither of which is in the year-1 flows (year-1 margin is ex-refund and ex-reinvestment). Q2 10-Q lines 1461, 1537, 1547.

historical_growth.basis: Continuing operations (standalone Dollar Tree) only, years ended Jan-2023 (CSV FY2023) to Jan-2026 (CSV FY2026). Five-year figures are not computed: the pre-FY2023 history is combined-company including Family Dollar and is not comparable.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: standalone revenue 3yr CAGR (8.0%), haircut to 5.0% for decelerating comps and unit growth
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable as a growth anchor: shareholders' equity fell from 8,751 to 3,755 over three years because of the Family Dollar goodwill/intangible impairments, the loss on sale and ~3.1B of buybacks -- not because the business shrank. EPS CAGRs are omitted for the same reason (reported EPS includes discontinued-operations losses of -4.54 and -14.03). Owner-FCF CAGR (15.5%) is flattered by a low FY2023 base (capex of only 639 that year) and runs ahead of reported-FCF CAGR because SBC plus award taxes fell from 140 to 72.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF grew faster than reported FCF over the window, i.e. SBC is a shrinking share of cash flow (0.9% of revenue in FY2023, 0.37% in FY2026; FY2025 was inflated by accelerated vesting of the former CEO's option award).

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone Dollar Tree delivers the guided year (net sales ~$20.6B, comps 3-4%) and then decelerates as multi-price ticket gains annualise: unit growth of ~3-4% net plus low-single-digit comps fades from 5.5% to a 2.5% terminal rate. Underlying operating margin holds around 9.2-9.5% -- the ex-refund level implied by guidance -- with the roll-off of Family Dollar transition-services income and ongoing price reinvestment offset by corporate SG&A right-sizing and shrink improvement. It does not get back to the 10.6% of the year ended Feb-2024. Capex intensity normalises from 5.6% to 4.2% of sales once the Phoenix and Marietta distribution centres are complete. The tariff refund is treated as a one-off worth only its ~$115M after-tax net benefit.
scenario_narratives.bull: Multi-price works as intended: higher-ticket items lift average ticket for several more years without costing traffic, the trade-down tailwind persists, and reinvested refund dollars buy durable share from Dollar General, Five Below and the online discounters. Sales compound at 6-6.5% for three years. Operating margin rebuilds to ~10.5% (pre-SBC EBITDA 14.8%), back at the standalone level of the year ended Feb-2024, as tariff costs stay lower after the IEEPA ruling, shrink keeps improving and the stranded Family Dollar corporate cost base is removed.
scenario_narratives.bear: The tariff regime turns against a business that direct-imports ~40% of its purchases, mostly from China (Section 122 or successor tariffs stick and cannot be passed through at low price points), while the multi-price move blurs the value proposition and traffic -- already -1.0% and +0.4% in the last two quarters -- turns negative. Comps go flat, growth falls to store additions only, and the price reinvestment funded this year by refunds becomes a permanent margin give-up: operating margin settles near 7.5% (pre-SBC EBITDA 11.8%), roughly a point below the year ended Jan-2026. Low-income consumer stress or SNAP cuts would push the same way. The business stays solidly cash-generative; this is a margin and growth bear, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Dollar Tree is valued as the standalone single-banner retailer it has been since July 2025, on continuing-operations cash flow only. The headline risk in reading this stock today is mistaking a refund-inflated year for earnings power: reported fiscal-2026 EPS guidance of $7.70-8.05 contains ~$0.60 of net tariff-refund benefit, and first-half operating cash flow contains $383M of refund cash. The model builds from the ex-refund margin (~9.3% operating) and a 5.1% owner-FCF margin, lets capex intensity fall as the distribution-centre build completes, and credits the refund only at its after-tax net value. SBC is small (~0.45% of revenue), so the house and street values sit close together and SBC treatment is not what drives the conclusion. Aggressive buybacks shrink the share count but are value-neutral here; they are not a source of intrinsic value at prices above it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin durability: each 1pt of sustained operating margin is worth roughly $14 per share; the gap between base (9.2%) and the year-ended-Feb-2024 level (10.6%) is the main upside lever, and tariff pass-through is the main downside one.
Terminal capex intensity: the model assumes capex falls from 5.6% to 4.2% of sales. If store growth and refresh keep it at ~5.5%, base value falls by roughly a fifth.
Cash tax shelter: the Family Dollar loss and bonus depreciation are holding cash taxes far below the 24.8% effective rate; a longer shelter than the two years modelled adds a few dollars per share.
Guidance-year execution: Q3 is guided to adjusted EPS of $0.80-0.95 on reinvestment spend. If the reinvestment has to continue beyond this year to hold comps, the base margin path is too high.
Balance-sheet vintage: net debt and shares are at 2026-08-01, six months into forecast year 1; buybacks since then lower both cash and the count.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 85.88-148.54
data_sources.financials: DLTR_Metrics.csv / core_metrics for revenue, EBITDA, SBC, debt, cash; continuing-operations OCF, capex, award taxes, cash taxes and guidance read from DLTR_Annual_FY2026.txt (10-K, year ended 2026-01-31), DLTR_Annual_FY2025.txt and DLTR_Quarterly_Q2-2027.txt (10-Q, quarter ended 2026-08-01)

inputs.share_count_basis: 187.67M shares issued and outstanding at 2026-08-01 (Q2 10-Q balance sheet) plus ~0.35M treasury-method dilution from share-based awards (Q2 EPS note) = 188.0M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: FY ended 2026-01-31 10-K cash flow statement, continuing operations: stock-based compensation expense 58.9 plus cash paid for taxes on exercises/vesting of stock-based compensation 13.3 (financing). No combined company figure is published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST), ERP ~4.75%, beta ~0.9 for a defensive value retailer gives cost of equity ~8.6-9.0%; funded debt is only ~7% of enterprise value at ~4% after tax. 8.5% applied to all three scenarios -- scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and the weights, not by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is an operating expense already inside EBITDA, so the lease cost is charged in the flows. Operating lease liabilities (4,737.3 at 2026-08-01) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is not used.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (capex intensity is still normalising from a distribution-centre and store build-out, so the owner-FCF margin has not matured by year 5). Standard US operating company; routed via dcf-methods table. First valuation of this ticker. PERIOD LABELS: the CSV labels fiscal years by the calendar year in which they END -- FY0 'FY2026' is the 52 weeks ended 2026-01-31, which the company calls 'fiscal 2025'. Year 1 of the forecast is the year ending ~2027-01-30, which the company calls 'fiscal 2026' and for which it has guided net sales of $20.5-20.7B and adjusted EPS of $7.70-8.05. STRUCTURAL BREAK: Family Dollar was sold on 2025-07-05. Everything here is built on continuing-operations (standalone Dollar Tree) figures for the years ended Jan-2023 to Jan-2026 as restated in the 10-Ks; the pre-divestiture combined-company history is not used for the FCF base, margins or growth. FCF BASE: owner FCF for the year ended 2026-01-31 = continuing-ops OCF 2,190.7 - capex 1,134.0 - SBC incl. equity-award taxes 72.2 = 984.5 (5.1% of revenue). That year contains no tariff refund. The CSV free_cash_flow column is blank for FY2025/FY2026 because the consolidated cash flow statement mixes discontinued operations; the continuing-ops lines were read off the 10-K. TARIFF REFUND NORMALISATION: 368.7 of IEEPA tariff refunds (383 cash including ~14 of interest) were received in the quarter ended 2026-08-01 and sit inside H1 OCF of 1,565.5 -- that half-year is NOT used as a base. The year-1 EBITDA margin is built ex-refund and ex-reinvestment from guided adjusted EPS less the ~$0.60 net refund benefit management disclosed. Because the 2026-08-01 balance sheet already holds the gross refund cash, the equity bridge deducts the part that does not accrue to owners (committed H2 reinvestment in price, marketing, store conditions and a ~$40M philanthropic fund, plus tax on the refund), leaving only the ~$115M after-tax net benefit. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped -- the company is in net debt, interest income is ~3 a year. BUYBACKS: an active repurchaser (1,548 in the year to Jan-2026, 1,209 in H1 incl. a 500 block from Mantle Ridge-affiliated holders), far above the SBC charge; the flat count is funded many times over and the excess is value-neutral in this model. TRANSITION SERVICES INCOME from Family Dollar (38.8 net in H1) is inside operating income and is assumed to roll off in year 2. PRICE is the last regular close; the next catalyst is Q3 results (late November 2026), guided to adjusted EPS of only $0.80-0.95 on reinvestment spend.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Margin is EBITDA BEFORE stock compensation (operating income + D&A + SBC). FY0 actual: 8.5% + 3.34% + 0.30% = 12.2%. Year 1 is ex-refund and ex-reinvestment: guided adjusted EPS midpoint 7.875 less 0.60 net refund benefit = ~7.28 x ~191M average shares = ~1,390 net income, ~1,850 pre-tax, ~1,915 operating income on ~20,600 revenue = 9.3%, cross-checked against H1 (1,163.4 - 368.7 refund + 22 reinvestment markdowns = 816.7, 8.3% in the seasonally weak half vs 6.7% a year earlier). Plus D&A ~3.6% and SBC ~0.4% = ~13.2%. Year 2 dips as Family Dollar transition-services income (~0.35% of revenue) rolls off and some price reinvestment persists; then slow SG&A leverage to 13.5%, an operating margin of ~9.2% -- well short of the 10.6% standalone margin of the year ended Feb-2024.
base.capex_note: Year 1 is guidance: $1.1-1.2B. Intensity falls as the Phoenix and Marietta distribution centres complete and unit growth slows; terminal 4.2% against D&A of 3.9% leaves room for ~2.5% growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Effective rate is 24.8%. Cash taxes paid were only 141 in FY0 (8.7% of pre-tax income) and H1 current tax was ~8% of pre-tax, because of losses realised on the Family Dollar sale and bonus depreciation. That shelter is not perpetual: 15% in year 1, 21% in year 2, statutory-equivalent 24.5% thereafter.
base.wc_capture_note: Negative: a retailer whose inventory (2,452) exceeds payables (1,627) consumes cash as it grows. Net operating working capital is ~4% of revenue; 3% is used because the shelf-productivity programme is taking inventory down while sales grow.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): tariff policy is unresolved and the company's import exposure is unusually concentrated, and traffic has already flattened. Base 50%: it is anchored on current guidance and the ex-refund run-rate. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs multi-price to keep working, tariffs to stay benign and the corporate cost base to come out, which are partly independent.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
